planting.note: Start seed or pot up young plants in early fall so growth is active through the cool winter rainfall period, then withhold water through summer dormancy.

directions: This is the sole species in its genus, forming pairs of thick, pale greenish-pink to whitish bodies that resemble a split pebble, native to the arid Richtersveld/southern Namibia border region. Grow in a mineral, fast-draining mix and keep completely dry through the hot summer months, resuming light watering only as nights cool in autumn. White to pale pink daisy-like flowers appear in autumn, often opening in the afternoon. Protect from frost and overhead watering, which can cause the bodies to split or rot.
sources: Smith, G.F. et al., Mesembs of the World (Briza Publications)

planting.note: Plant offsets or divisions in early fall to establish roots ahead of the winter growing season typical of South African mesembs.

directions: A low, mat-forming South African succulent with small, triangular, grayish-green leaves held in dense clusters. It produces bright yellow, daisy-like flowers that open in sunlight during the cooler months. Grow in shallow, gritty soil with excellent drainage and reduce watering sharply in summer to mimic its native winter-rainfall habitat. Clumps spread slowly by offsetting and can be divided to propagate new plants.
sources: Smith, G.F. et al., Mesembs of the World (Briza Publications)

planting.note: Establish divisions or rooted offsets in early fall to coincide with the start of active winter growth.

directions: This South African mesemb forms dense clusters of short, fleshy, three-angled leaves arising from numerous crowded heads, true to its name. Bright yellow, many-petaled flowers open in the afternoon sun during the cool season. It prefers a gritty, fast-draining substrate and a near-complete rest with minimal water during summer dormancy. Clumps can be gently separated and replanted to increase stock.
sources: Smith, G.F. et al., Mesembs of the World (Briza Publications)

planting.note: Pot up seedlings or young plants in early fall to align growth with the natural autumn-to-spring active period.

directions: Native to the Eastern Cape of South Africa, this small shrubby mesemb produces thick leaf pairs fused at the base into a distinctive triangular or rhomboid cross-section. Bright yellow flowers open on sunny afternoons during the cooler growing months. It needs very sharp drainage and should be kept almost entirely dry in summer to avoid rot. Older plants develop a short woody base as new leaf pairs replace the old each season.
sources: Smith, G.F. et al., Mesembs of the World (Briza Publications)
